purpose: Environment concept art and map-selection artwork. These images do not implement playable terrain or collision geometry.

assets.name: frostgate
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: finished environment illustration for a new Noordheim tactical RTS level, suitable for a map-selection card and landscape art reference.
Style/medium: premium stylized 3D low-poly render, carefully faceted granite and terrain, chunky evergreen silhouettes, matte materials, rich ambient occlusion, tiny weathered red Scandinavian timber military structures with charcoal pitched roofs and restrained olive-drab modern field equipment. Cohesive handcrafted miniature-world aesthetic. Nordic near-future setting, no fantasy architecture.
Composition: landscape 16:9 image, high oblique orthographic RTS camera, show a whole coherent traversable battlefield with readable roads, natural chokepoints, open base-building clearings, layered elevation and believable terrain transitions. Landscape extends to image edges, no floating diorama slab, no sky or horizon. Terrain is the hero; buildings and vehicles are sparse small-scale environmental details. Detailed, polished game environment art with crisp silhouettes and subtle texture.
Constraints: no lettering, labels, logos, symbols, UI, grids, borders, watermarks or inset panels. One continuous scene, not a collage.
Primary request: FROSTGATE — a glacier mountain pass, visually dominated by chalk-white snowfields and deep cyan glacial ice, cobalt meltwater and slate mountains. A sinuous glacial ravine divides two broad snow-covered terraces; a single sturdy utilitarian steel bridge crosses the central ravine, with a longer switchback route around its shallow upstream end. Dark exposed bedrock and carefully placed ice cliffs distinguish impassable terrain from broad packed-snow routes. Sparse wind-stunted spruce, a small red-timber research outpost and ore yard on a level shelf, a couple of tiny winter-camouflaged utility trucks. Foreground ice boulders frame the map without blocking the road. Cold clear daylight, gentle warm sun on rock edges, blue shadows, physically coherent readable terrain. Strongly alpine and glacial rather than a generic snowy forest.

Primary request: AMBERFEN — a Nordic autumn marsh delta, visually dominated by rich amber reeds, rust-orange birch canopies, olive peat islands and muted green-blue water. Several narrow slow river channels braid through the low flat wetland, separating broad dry islands with generous base clearings; raised gravel causeways, two low timber-and-steel bridges and a shallow pebbled ford make a legible asymmetric loop route. Scattered dark spruce contrast with deciduous autumn groves, lichen granite outcrops, flooded reed beds and muddy wheel tracks. A tiny weathered red-timber pumping station and timber supply yard on high ground, one or two olive field vehicles. Soft low autumn sunlight and restrained wisps of ground mist at distant edges, still crisp and readable. No snow, no glaciers, no volcanic elements. Strong wetland identity and clear dry-versus-wet boundaries.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.

Primary request: CINDERREACH — a rugged Nordic volcanic black-sand coast, visually dominated by charcoal basalt, deep petrol-teal surf and rust-red geothermal earth with pale sulfur-ochre accents. A crescent of black beach and a rocky tidal inlet occupy one side; inland angular basalt escarpments form two broad dark ash terraces connected by a winding industrial gravel ramp, while a second wider road loops behind a geothermal basin. Tall hexagonal basalt columns and sparse moss mark cliff edges, thin steam plumes rise from a few milky turquoise geothermal pools, weathered red-timber utility huts and a small corrugated-metal geothermal works sit on a flat buildable shelf. A couple tiny olive industrial vehicles provide scale. Silver overcast coastal light with a subtle warm break through clouds, restrained atmosphere, sharp terrain readability. No lava rivers, no erupting volcano, no snow, almost treeless. The level feels grounded in Icelandic geology and clearly distinct from snow and autumn wetland maps.
